sourceObservations.observation: A random named database is reserved in a fresh explicit evidence directory before CREATE. The created flag follows the successful CREATE acknowledgement. Only the named database and mkdtemp-owned directory are cleanup targets; local admin URL is constrained to loopback /postgres. A failed/unknown start cannot enter successful cleanup because required journey facts are missing.

The proxy forwards the original key and exact empty JSON body, fully reads a successful center response with matching task identity and cancellation status, durably saves ack-drop.json, then destroys the downstream response. It does not simulate acceptance merely by dropping an outbound request.

The first scenario closes and reopens the same private journal after B is admitted publicly, verifies reopening sends no cancellation, and explicitly recovers the saved A key/path/body. It checks B remains running and the saved request clears only after acceptance.

The driver starts the real TUI entry on a PTY, types the open/cancel commands, waits for visible cancellation, receives C identity after the parent verifies B termination and admits C, types CJK and multiline draft text, resizes, then sends Ctrl-C. The scenario checks that C remains running after terminal exit, no C cancellation was sent, and explicitly releases the synthetic C barrier to finish.

The Python driver is a detached owned process-group leader; the TUI inherits that group. Parent cleanup checks group existence and applies bounded TERM/KILL windows, independently of the direct child exit. Unknown stop marks failure and prevents success cleanup. This is a fixture process-group check, not a claim about arbitrary native descendants or OS containment.

Cleanup collects task state, stops owned resources, observes no database consumers, and writes/fsyncs a checkpoint before DROP DATABASE or recursive removal. Missing journey facts, shutdown unknown, failed evidence write or test failure retain database/tmp. Each evidence file is exclusive-create and bounded to 2 MiB. The checkpoint remains available if a later cleanup/result write fails.

limits: This is source review only, not APPROVED runtime acceptance. Tests, imports/typecheck, HTTP, PG, PTY, browser and provider were not run by this reviewer or for this new three-file target.
The previous 36 passing checks apply to the earlier controller/Ink slice and do not validate these three new files.
Fresh resource admission and the installed dependency closure must be checked by the execution owner before any run; this review does not grant a PG/PTY window.

Timeout wrappers only bound waiting; they do not prove that an arbitrary in-process operation has stopped. The source retains recovery data on unknown rather than treating timeout as settlement. Actual lifecycle and cleanup must be recorded in the eventual run.
CJK/resize/multiline/raw-mode observations are proposed assertions, not measured results. The raw-mode assertion compares ICANON/ECHO flags, not the entire termios structure.
This synthetic recognized-session adapter does not exercise an SDK/provider or prove native/A2A cancellation. No actual App/browser driver or cross-client visible App acceptance is included.
No production source, author files, dependencies, Git state or live services were modified. Only these reviewer /tmp JSON receipts were written.

methods.applied: Read the finite fixture lifetime and public-consumer boundaries, follow cancellation/error paths, verify immutable source bindings, and distinguish pending behavior assertions from evidence. No new framework or source changes requested.
